scope: Development-only Fixed/Elastic/Free comparison on one 28-vCPU host; no cross-host or Terminal-Bench population claim.

execution.retry_policy: No automatic retry. Preserve a failed arm and stop the schedule.

amendments.visible_result: Block 1 Fixed completed; the first Elastic attempt reached 30/32 before termination.
amendments.reason: The original 1-to-2 CPU and 2-to-2.5 GiB envelope left idle host capacity unavailable to long-running tasks and did not test meaningful elasticity on the 28-vCPU host.
amendments.action: Preserve and exclude the partial Elastic artifact, then rerun Elastic with a 1-to-8 CPU and 2-to-16 GiB per-task envelope under the unchanged 24 CPU and 60 GiB shared pool.

followups.name: elastic-max24
followups.question: Was Free faster primarily because Elastic capped each task at 8 CPU cores?
followups.configuration: Initial 1 CPU and 2 GiB per task; maximum 24 CPU and 16 GiB per task; shared pool unchanged at 24 CPU and 60 GiB.

followups.name: quota-only-c1
followups.question: Can a full initial cpuset keep nproc-based build parallelism available while EAR controls actual CPU time only through quota?
followups.configuration: magsac-install and build-linux-kernel-qemu only; concurrency 1; cpuset 0-23 from container start; dynamic 1-to-24 CPU quota and 2-to-16 GiB memory; shared pool 24 CPU and 60 GiB.

followups.name: quota-only-c16
followups.question: Does quota-only CPU elasticity retain the c1 mechanism benefit under the original 32-trace, concurrency-16 contention?
followups.configuration: Original 32-trace manifest and concurrency 16; cpuset 0-23 from container start; dynamic 1-to-24 CPU quota and 2-to-16 GiB memory; shared pool 24 CPU and 60 GiB.

followups.name: quota-only-no-guard-c8
followups.question: Does disabling the marginal-growth guard let long-running survivors grow again when contested CPU capacity becomes available?
followups.configuration: The eight long-tail tasks from quota-only-c16 at concurrency 8; quota-only CPU elasticity with marginal_growth_min_cores set to zero; shared pool unchanged at 24 CPU and 60 GiB.

followup_results.name: quota-only-c1
followup_results.interpretation: Mechanism gate passed: nproc reported 24 with an initial one-core quota, both tasks reached about 24 observed cores, both succeeded, and all leases were released without OOM or resize rejection.

followup_results.name: quota-only-c16
followup_results.observed_integral_method: Sum of each resources.json arithmetic sample mean times its monitored duration.
followup_results.mechanism_evidence: magsac-install launched 24-way builds but remained at a two-core quota for 1218.5 continuous seconds after its last early grow; after every other container had exited it still remained at two cores for about 763 seconds. Its OpenCV build then hit the 600-second tool timeout. Full initial CPU visibility is necessary for nproc-based commands but is insufficient while the v2 marginal-growth guard suppresses retries after an early contention-limited probe.

followup_results.name: quota-only-no-guard-c8
followup_results.observed_integral_method: Sum of each container resource summary arithmetic sample mean times its monitored duration.
followup_results.mechanism_evidence: The survivor growth path was restored: magsac-install grew 2-to-4 at 247.0 seconds, 4-to-8 at 334.1 seconds, 8-to-16 at 455.9 seconds, and 16-to-24 at 541.2 seconds as capacity became available. llm-spec-decoding reached eight cores by 10.7 seconds. Both previously source-valid replay failures succeeded, with no OOM, admission failure, memory resize rejection, or leaked lease.
followup_results.limitation: This targeted eight-task concurrency-8 probe reuses the long-tail cohort from the earlier 32-task concurrency-16 run. Per-task mechanism outcomes are informative, but aggregate wall time and throughput are not a matched arm comparison. Disabling the guard also caused 714 controller-level global-pool-exhausted retry rejections.
